title: Brief to Live: four extra takes that save a reshoot
hook: Most people see the ad. Almost nobody sees the shoot day.
caption:
Most people see the ad. Almost nobody sees the shoot day.

A reshoot is usually decided on the shoot itself, by what did not get filmed.

So the plan for the day carries four extra takes besides the main one:

1. Three openings for the same script, because the opening is the first thing to test.
2. The product up close, label readable, held still.
3. The approved claim, word for word, in one clean take. An edit cannot repair a paraphrased claim.
4. Ten seconds of the room with nobody talking, to cover cuts.

Tick all four before the creator packs up. After that, each missing one is a second shoot day.

Brief to Live is a series on what happens between the brief and the ad going live.

script.setup: Idea: a brand or creative manager loses days to reshoots because the shoot captured only the main take. On-screen title (first frame): 'The shoot day nobody sees'. Expectation it sets: a look behind a creator shoot. The first line meets it; the video beats it with four extra takes to film so the edit rarely needs a reshoot. Order: two easy takes first, then a re-hook, then the claim take, which matters most. Shot vertically on a phone during a real creator shoot, with permission. Blur faces, product names and brand names unless cleared.

scenes.visual: A creator setting up a phone on a tripod at home. Title text sits on the first frame.
scenes.voiceover: Everybody sees the ad. Here is the shoot day behind it.

scenes.visual: A printed shot list on a table with four lines under the main take.
scenes.voiceover: Most plan for one good take. Plan four extra ones and you rarely need a reshoot.

scenes.visual: The creator says a first line to camera three different ways, shown as three quick cuts.
scenes.voiceover: One. Three openings for the same script. The opening is what gets tested first.

scenes.visual: Close shot of a product held still in a hand, label facing the camera (blurred if not cleared).
scenes.voiceover: Two. The product up close, label readable, held still.

scenes.visual: Shrutik to camera, holding the shot list.
scenes.voiceover: Those are easy. The next one saves the most trouble.

scenes.visual: The brief on a phone with one line highlighted. The creator reads it, then says it to camera.
scenes.voiceover: Three. The approved claim, word for word. An edit cannot fix a paraphrase.

scenes.visual: The empty room, camera still rolling, nobody speaking.
scenes.voiceover: Four. Ten seconds of the room, nobody talking. It covers every cut.

scenes.visual: A hand ticks four boxes on the shot list while the tripod is folded in the background.
scenes.voiceover: Tick all four before the creator packs up.

scenes.visual: Shrutik to camera. Galvor logo end card.
scenes.voiceover: A good shoot leaves the edit with choices. Follow Galvor for more.
